speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with a generalized rash; to help you, I need to ask a few questions. Can you tell me if this rash appeared immediately after birth or a few days later?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash is noted to be present for only 1 day in a 4-day-old newborn, while the mother has a history of gonorrhea. Did anyone notice pustular lesions or any discharge from the eyes during the first day of life?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) infection.

The presence of a maculopapular rash with pustules on an erythematous base, sparing the palms and soles, in a 4-day-old with maternal history of genital infections is highly suggestive of disseminated neonatal HSV or cutaneous HSV. I am requesting immediate results for HSV PCR from the blood and swab of the rash lesion.
